lines.text: White light looks simple. It isn't.
Send it through glass, and it comes apart: every colour it was carrying, side by side.
Red bends the least. Violet bends the most.
A surface moves, and light gathers into bright, living lines.
One drop, and the pattern breaks, rings out, and knits itself back together.
Glass can gather light, as well as split it.
A sphere becomes a lens, and the light it gathers burns to a single point.
Even now, the lens in your eye is bending light, to show you this.
